questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A function f : R₊ → R (where R₊ is the set of all non-negative real numbers) defined by f(x) = 4x + 3 is :
questions.solution: 4x + 3 = 4y + 3 gives x = y, so f is one-one. For x ≥ 0, f(x) ≥ 3, so values below 3 are never taken: not onto.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If a matrix has 36 elements, the number of possible orders it can have is :
questions.solution: An order m × n needs mn = 36. 36 has 9 divisors (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36), so there are 9 orders.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Which of the following statements is true for the function f(x) = x² + 3 for x ≠ 0 and f(x) = 1 for x = 0?
options: f(x) is continuous and differentiable ∀ x ∈ R
f(x) is continuous and differentiable ∀ x ∈ R − {0}
f(x) is discontinuous at infinitely many points
questions.solution: lim(x→0) f(x) = 3 ≠ f(0) = 1, so f is discontinuous only at 0; elsewhere it is a polynomial, hence continuous and differentiable.

questions.text: If A and B are two non-zero square matrices of the same order such that (A + B)² = A² + B², then :
questions.solution: (A + B)² = A² + AB + BA + B², so AB + BA = O, i.e. AB = −BA.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): For the matrix A = [[1, cos θ, 1], [−cos θ, 1, cos θ], [−1, −cos θ, 1]], where θ ∈ [0, 2π], |A| ∈ [2, 4].
Reason (R): cos θ ∈ [−1, 1], ∀ θ ∈ [0, 2π].
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Expanding, |A| = (1 + cos²θ) − cos θ(−cos θ + cos θ) + (cos²θ + 1) = 2 + 2cos²θ. Since cos θ ∈ [−1, 1], cos²θ ∈ [0, 1] and |A| ∈ [2, 4]. Both true, and R explains A.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): A line in space cannot be drawn perpendicular to the x, y and z axes simultaneously.
Reason (R): For any line making angles α, β, γ with the positive directions of the x, y and z axes respectively, cos²α + cos²β + cos²γ = 1.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Perpendicular to all three axes would need cos α = cos β = cos γ = 0, contradicting cos²α + cos²β + cos²γ = 1. Both true, and R explains A.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Check whether the function f(x) = x²|x| is differentiable at x = 0 or not.
questions.solution: f(x) = x³ for x ≥ 0 and −x³ for x < 0. Left and right derivatives at 0: lim (f(h) − f(0))/h = lim h|h| = 0 from both sides. So f is differentiable at 0 with f′(0) = 0.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If y = √(tan √x), prove that √x dy/dx = (1 + y⁴)/(4y).
questions.solution: y² = tan √x, so 2y dy/dx = sec²√x · 1/(2√x). Hence √x dy/dx = sec²√x/(4y) = (1 + tan²√x)/(4y) = (1 + y⁴)/(4y).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Show that the function f(x) = 4x³ − 18x² + 27x − 7 has neither maxima nor minima.
questions.solution: f′(x) = 12x² − 36x + 27 = 3(2x − 3)² ≥ 0. It vanishes only at x = 3/2 and does not change sign there, so f is increasing throughout and has no maximum or minimum.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If a and b are two non-zero vectors such that (a + b) ⊥ a and (2a + b) ⊥ b, then prove that |b| = √2 |a|.
questions.solution: (a + b)·a = 0 gives |a|² + a·b = 0, so a·b = −|a|². (2a + b)·b = 0 gives 2a·b + |b|² = 0, so |b|² = 2|a|² and |b| = √2|a|.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: ABCD is a parallelogram. If AB = 2i − 4j + 5k and DB = 3i − 6j + 2k, then find AD and hence find the area of parallelogram ABCD.
questions.solution: AB = AD + DB, so AD = AB − DB = −i + 2j + 3k. AB × AD = (−12 − 10)i − (6 + 5)j + (4 − 4)k = −22i − 11j. Area = |AB × AD| = √(484 + 121) = 11√5 square units.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A relation R on the set A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} is defined as R = {(x, y) : |x² − y²| < 8}. Check whether the relation R is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
questions.solution: Reflexive: |x² − x²| = 0 < 8. Symmetric: |y² − x²| = |x² − y²|. Not transitive: (1, 2) ∈ R (|1 − 4| = 3) and (2, 3) ∈ R (|4 − 9| = 5), but (1, 3) ∉ R since |1 − 9| = 8.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A function f is defined from R → R as f(x) = ax + b, such that f(1) = 1 and f(2) = 3. Find the function f(x). Hence, check whether f(x) is one-one and onto or not.
questions.solution: a + b = 1 and 2a + b = 3 give a = 2, b = −1, so f(x) = 2x − 1. 2x₁ − 1 = 2x₂ − 1 gives x₁ = x₂ (one-one); any y ∈ R is f((y + 1)/2) (onto).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If √(1 − x²) + √(1 − y²) = a(x − y), prove that dy/dx = √((1 − y²)/(1 − x²)).
questions.solution: Put x = sin A, y = sin B: cos A + cos B = a(sin A − sin B) gives cot((A − B)/2) = a, so sin⁻¹x − sin⁻¹y = 2cot⁻¹a, a constant. Differentiating, dy/dx = √(1 − y²)/√(1 − x²).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If y = (tan x)ˣ, then find dy/dx.
questions.solution: log y = x log tan x. Differentiating: (1/y) dy/dx = log tan x + x sec²x/tan x. So dy/dx = (tan x)ˣ [log tan x + x sec²x/tan x] = (tan x)ˣ [log tan x + 2x cosec 2x].

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the particular solution of the differential equation x² dy/dx − xy = x² cos²(y/(2x)), given that when x = 1, y = π/2.
questions.solution: dy/dx = y/x + cos²(y/(2x)). Put y = vx: x dv/dx = cos²(v/2), so sec²(v/2) dv = dx/x and 2 tan(v/2) = log|x| + C. At x = 1, v = π/2: 2 = C. Particular solution: 2 tan(y/(2x)) = log|x| + 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: AA⁻¹ = I. Row 1 × column 3: −1 − 5a + 6 = 0, so a = 1. Row 1 × column 1: −1 − 8a + 2b = 1, so b = 5. Row 1 × column 2: 1 + 7a + 2y = 0, so y = −4. Row 2 × column 3: 1 − 10 + 3x = 0, so x = 3. (a + x) − (b + y) = 4 − 1 = 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Evaluate : ∫ from 0 to π/4 of (sin x + cos x)/(9 + 16 sin 2x) dx
questions.solution: Put t = sin x − cos x, dt = (cos x + sin x) dx, sin 2x = 1 − t²; limits −1 to 0. Integral = ∫₋₁⁰ dt/(25 − 16t²) = (1/40)[log|(5 + 4t)/(5 − 4t)|]₋₁⁰ = (1/40)(0 − log(1/9)) = (1/20) log 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Evaluate : ∫ from 0 to π/2 of sin 2x tan⁻¹(sin x) dx
questions.solution: sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x; put t = sin x: ∫₀¹ 2t tan⁻¹t dt = [t² tan⁻¹t]₀¹ − ∫₀¹ t²/(1 + t²) dt = π/4 − (1 − π/4) = π/2 − 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The image of the point P(x, y, z) with respect to the line x/1 = (y − 1)/2 = (z − 2)/3 is P′(1, 0, 7). Find the coordinates of the point P.
questions.solution: Let M(λ, 1 + 2λ, 2 + 3λ) be the foot of the perpendicular from P′. P′M = (λ − 1, 1 + 2λ, 3λ − 5) ⊥ (1, 2, 3): 14λ − 14 = 0, so λ = 1 and M = (1, 3, 5). M is the mid-point of PP′, so P = 2M − P′ = (1, 6, 3).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
The traffic police has installed an Over Speed Violation Detection (OSVD) system at various locations in a city. These cameras can capture a speeding vehicle from a distance of 300 m and even function in the dark. A camera is installed on a pole at a height of 5 m. It detects a car travelling away from the pole at a speed of 20 m/s. At any point x m away from the base of the pole, the angle of elevation of the speed camera from the car C is θ.

Express θ in terms of the height of the camera installed on the pole and x.
questions.solution: tan θ = 5/x, so θ = tan⁻¹(5/x).

It detects a car travelling away from the pole at a speed of 20 m/s. At any point x m away from the base of the pole, the angle of elevation of the speed camera from the car C is θ.

Find the rate of change of the angle of elevation with respect to time at an instant when the car is 50 m away from the pole.
questions.solution: dθ/dt = (dθ/dx)(dx/dt) = −5/(2500 + 25) × 20 = −100/2525 = −4/101 rad/s. The angle decreases at 4/101 rad/s.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
If a function f : X → Y defined as f(x) = y is one-one and onto, then we can define a unique function g : Y → X such that g(y) = x, where x ∈ X and y = f(x), y ∈ Y. Function g is called the inverse of function f. The domain of the sine function is R and sine : R → R is neither one-one nor onto. Let the sine function be defined from a set A to [−1, 1] such that the inverse of the sine function exists, i.e. sin⁻¹x is defined from [−1, 1] to A.

If A is an interval other than the principal value branch, give an example of one such interval.
questions.solution: For example [π/2, 3π/2] (or [−3π/2, −π/2]).

Function g is called the inverse of function f. The domain of the sine function is R and sine : R → R is neither one-one nor onto. Let the sine function be defined from a set A to [−1, 1] such that the inverse of the sine function exists, i.e. sin⁻¹x is defined from [−1, 1] to A.

Draw the graph of sin⁻¹x from [−1, 1] to its principal value branch.
questions.solution: An increasing curve from (−1, −π/2) through the origin to (1, π/2); it is the reflection of y = sin x on [−π/2, π/2] in the line y = x.

Function g is called the inverse of function f. The domain of the sine function is R and sine : R → R is neither one-one nor onto. Let the sine function be defined from a set A to [−1, 1] such that the inverse of the sine function exists, i.e. sin⁻¹x is defined from [−1, 1] to A.

Find the domain and range of f(x) = 2 sin⁻¹(1 − x).
questions.solution: −1 ≤ 1 − x ≤ 1 gives domain [0, 2]. sin⁻¹ takes values in [−π/2, π/2], so the range is [−π, π].
